SEARCH
Package org.aristonis.diwan.database.schema

Class Schema

java.lang.Object
org.aristonis.diwan.database.schema.Schema
public final class Schema extends Object
Creates, changes and inspects tables, as Laravel's Schema facade does.

A schema pairs a Connection with the SchemaGrammar of its database: 


 Schema schema = Schema.of(db, new SQLiteSchemaGrammar());
 schema.create("users", table -> {
     table.id();
     table.string("email").unique();
     table.timestamps();
 });

The connection's table prefix is added to every table name. Each call checks its blueprint before any SQL runs. When a call produces several statements, they run in one transaction if the connection is not in one yet and the database can undo schema changes; otherwise they run one by one, and those before a failure stay applied.

On SQLite, adding or dropping a primary or foreign key on an existing table rebuilds the table. Outside a transaction the schema builder runs the rebuild through withoutForeignKeyConstraints(Consumer) on its own; inside one, a rebuild of a table other tables point at is refused with ForeignKeysOffRequiredException, because SQLite would apply their delete actions. The migrator catches it and runs that migration again with enforcement off.

Instances are immutable and as safe to share between threads as their connection.

    • withoutForeignKeyConstraints

      public void withoutForeignKeyConstraints(Consumer<Schema> work)
      Runs schema work in one transaction with foreign key enforcement switched off, as Laravel's Schema::withoutForeignKeyConstraints does.

      On SQLite the work runs on one physical connection with PRAGMA foreign_keys off, and the setting is put back afterwards; if it cannot be put back, that session is discarded instead of closed, so a driver that can abort the connection keeps it out of the pool. Rows the work writes are not checked against foreign keys, except those a table rebuild copies. In pretend mode the work only runs.

      Parameters:
      work - the work, given a schema builder for the switched-off connection, never null
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if work is null
      IllegalStateException - if the connection is inside a transaction
      RuntimeException - any failure of the work, after the transaction is undone

    • pretend

      public List<LoggedQuery> pretend(Consumer<Schema> work)
      Records the statements schema work would run, without changing the database.

      Unlike a schema builder made on a pretend connection, this one reads the live schema, so a change that depends on the table's current shape, such as a SQLite rebuild, lists its real statements. A table made earlier in the same pretend run does not exist yet for such a read.

      Parameters:
      work - the work, given a recording schema builder, never null
      Returns:
      the recorded statements in order, unmodifiable, never null
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if work is null
      RuntimeException - any failure of the work

    • dropAllTables

      public void dropAllTables()
      Drops every table that getTables() lists, as Laravel's Schema::dropAllTables does; nothing runs if there is none.

      Foreign keys between the dropped tables do not block the drop. Where the grammar needs several statements, they run in one transaction unless the connection is in one already, so a failure leaves every table in place. Internal tables, such as PostGIS's spatial_ref_sys, stay. Names are the real names, so the table prefix is not added again.

      Throws:
      UnsupportedOperationException - if the grammar cannot list or drop tables
      QueryException - if a statement fails

    • dropAllViews

      public void dropAllViews()
      Drops every view that getViews() lists, as Laravel's Schema::dropAllViews does; nothing runs if there is none.

      Statements run as in dropAllTables().

      Throws:
      UnsupportedOperationException - if the grammar cannot list or drop views
      QueryException - if a statement fails

    • statement

      public void statement(String sql)
      Runs one statement as given, for what the builder cannot say.

      Like the other calls, it runs on this schema's connection: inside a migration it joins the migration's transaction, and under pretend(Consumer) it is recorded, not run. The SQL is trusted, like an Expression: build it from constants only, never from user input. A migration that the migrator runs again with foreign keys off, after a SQLite table rebuild was refused, runs its statements again too, so keep them to the database.

      Parameters:
      sql - the statement, never null or blank
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if sql is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if sql is blank
      QueryException - if the statement fails
